text: The Perkin Medal is an annual award presented by the Society of Chemical Industry (American Section) to a scientist living in the United States for an "innovation in applied chemistry resulting in outstanding commercial development." It is recognized as the highest honor in the U.S. chemical industry. The medal was first awarded in 1906 to mark the 50th anniversary of the discovery of mauveine, the world's first synthetic aniline dye, by Sir William Henry Perkin, an English chemist. The award was given to Sir William during his visit to the United States the year before his death. It was subsequently awarded in 1908 and has been presented every year since then.
